newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to reopen probe into aid to GAN.
newsitem.headline: EU to reopen probe into aid to GAN.

text.p: The European Commission will reopen a state aid probe into Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) following the French government's announcement of a rescue package of up to 20 billion French francs ($3.5 billion) for the ailing insurer.
"We are going to open a procedure again," a Commission spokesman told reporters.
He said the Commission had been duly informed by the French government of the latest developments in the GAN case, but had not yet received the new rescue measures. He declined to comment further.
In September, the Commission cleared a 2.8 billion-franc capital injection into GAN by the French state in 1995 under a restructuring plan aimed at ensuring the company's long-term viability.
The plan involved the sale of GAN's non core assets such as its majority holding in Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC).
"They haven't succeeded (to sell CIC)," a Commission competition official said. He added: "Apparently, nobody is interested in buying it".
Paris announced on Thursday it would have to spend an additional 20 billion french francs to shore up the company's accounts after 35 billion francs of losses since 1992.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said the government would inject 11 billion francs into GAN this year, seven billion to cover losses at the UIC property unit which has run up losses of 30 billion francs in three years, and 3.9 billion francs for GAN Assurances.
The state could pay out another nine billion francs to cover losses on property loans and sales, Arthuis said.
GAN shares were suspended on the Paris exchange on Friday.
